question: Should queued webhook ingestion become a core Gateway feature now, and if so should https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100940's `hooks.queues` plus SQLite/RPC/UI shape be the accepted implementation path?
rationale: The request adds new core configuration, persistent state, an HTTP ingestion endpoint, operator RPC/UI surfaces, and concurrency semantics on a protected maintainer-labeled item, so automation should not choose the product/API direction without maintainer intent.

options.title: Review Linked Core PR
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers review the linked draft PR for config, schema, permission, UI, docs, and upgrade-safety shape.

options.title: Narrow To Concurrency Policy
options.body: Defer durable backlog storage and handle the immediate need through narrower hook lane or same-session admission policy work.

options.title: Defer From Core
options.body: Leave existing immediate hooks as the supported core path until a smaller plugin/API extension or stronger operator demand justifies core queueing.

recommendation.title: Review Linked Core PR
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers review the linked draft PR for config, schema, permission, UI, docs, and upgrade-safety shape.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent hook/session policy history and prior adjacent decisions make this the best available owner for the product/API shape question.
